ask: I've changed my mind about audit being a part of kmctl. kmctl is an optional component that should help people organize knowledge using coding agents. kmaudit should be its own library. Instead of a complex CLI, we should create an MCP server with stdio. kmaudit should work for any folder with markdown docs. A user can point it to 'docs', '.okf' etc. The audit should be independent from kmctl, except that obviously they work well together. Every folder should get its own namespace so that things don't clash. The CLI should only give access to the MCP or UI. Perhaps a couple of list commands to check a database, or something like list namespaces. Users can integrate kmaudit with various harnesses, e.g. claude, codex, antigravity and so on (also e.g. langgraph agents). The skills that we currently have stay, but they should point at the MCP. A briefing command should still be CLI-only. It could inject summary statistics from an existing kmaudit database.
